source_caption:
Russell Crowe makes Bud White feel terrifying before he ever says much in L.A. Confidential. The performance works because Crowe plays him as pure physical force on the surface, but slowly reveals a wounded, protective man underneath — turning what could have been a simple brutal cop into one of the film’s most tragic characters.

L.A. Confidential (1997), directed by Curtis Hanson, starring Kevin Spacey, Russell Crowe, Guy Pearce. A stylish and gripping neo-noir crime thriller that exposes corruption, ambition, and violence beneath the glamorous surface of 1950s Los Angeles.

source_details.synopsis: L.A. Confidential is a 1997 American neo-noir crime thriller film directed, produced, and co-written by Curtis Hanson. The screenplay, by Hanson and Brian Helgeland, is based on James Ellroy's 1990 novel, the third book in his L.A. Quartet series. The film tells the story of a group of LAPD officers in 1953, and the intersection of police corruption and Hollywood celebrity. The title refers to the 1950s scandal magazine Confidential, portrayed in the film as Hush-Hush. At the time, actors Guy Pearce and Russell Crowe were relatively unknown in North America.
